User Story: As a first-time user, I want RTI to open setup instead of dropping me into a blank app so I can become operational quickly.
Expected Behavior: If required keys are missing at launch, the onboarding window opens; otherwise RTI performs a quiet update check and continues into the app.
Notes: Manual verification blocked because the app aborts during NSApplication init before onboarding can render in this environment.

User Story: As a user, I want to save transcription and assistant keys locally so RTI can run live sessions.
Expected Behavior: Onboarding requires non-empty Soniox and active-LLM keys, writes them to the local credential store, verifies the write landed, and shows saved state or an error.
Notes: Onboarding text and storage flow updated for provider-aware keys on 2026-06-30.

User Story: As a user, I want RTI to guide microphone access so live transcription can start.
Expected Behavior: Onboarding shows microphone state, requests permission, reflects granted or denied state, and keeps readiness false until mic access is granted.

User Story: As a user, I want RTI to explain screen recording access so screenshot OCR works when I choose to use it.
Expected Behavior: Onboarding marks screen recording as optional, can trigger the request flow, and routes denied users to System Settings.

User Story: As a user, I want RTI to live in the menubar without a Dock icon so it stays unobtrusive during meetings.
Expected Behavior: The app is configured as a menubar accessory, installs its command/menu system on launch, and exposes window toggles from there.
Notes: Crash report `~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/RTI-2026-06-30-172212.ips` shows SIGABRT inside `NSApplication sharedApplication` / `_RegisterApplication`.

User Story: As a user, I want a second launch attempt to focus the existing RTI instance instead of opening duplicates.
Expected Behavior: If another RTI instance is already running, the earlier instance is activated and the new one terminates.

User Story: As a user, I want an About view so I can confirm what RTI is and where the project lives.
Expected Behavior: The About command opens the standard macOS about panel with RTI copy, credits, and repository link.

User Story: As a user, I want RTI to tell me when a newer signed build exists.
Expected Behavior: Manual checks show either up-to-date status or a download prompt for a newer GitHub release; normal launches only interrupt if a newer release exists.

User Story: As a user, I want to show or hide the overlay from anywhere so RTI is available without stealing focus.
Expected Behavior: The overlay is visible at install, can be toggled globally with Command-Backslash, and reopening the app with no visible windows shows it again.

User Story: As a user, I want the overlay excluded from screen captures and screen shares.
Expected Behavior: RTI persists an invisibility flag, applies sharingType protection to the overlay and floating panels, and lets the user toggle the state from commands and overlay UI.

User Story: As a user, I want quick opacity changes so I can tune legibility versus intrusiveness during a call.
Expected Behavior: The overlay more-menu exposes discrete opacity presets and writes the selected value to persisted overlay appearance settings.

User Story: As a user, I want to tune overlay light mode and size so the panel fits my screen and preference.
Expected Behavior: Settings expose light mode, width, height, and background opacity; changes notify the overlay to resize or redraw.

User Story: As a user, I want to open the Setup tab from the overlay chrome so I can configure project context, live panels, and discussion guides before recording.
Expected Behavior: The Setup affordance in the overlay should switch to the Setup tab, and the documented `⌘⌥0` hotkey should do the same.
Notes: Pixel click on the Setup pill and `⌘⌥0` both reached Setup on 2026-06-30; earlier AX failure appears specific to the automation action route, not the user-facing interaction.

User Story: As a user, I want one action to start or finish a live RTI session.
Expected Behavior: Start transitions idle or done into a fresh live session; stop finalizes capture, runs archive and summary flows, and blocks restart during finishing.
Entry Points: Command-Shift-R; menu; overlay more menu; Sentinel banner

User Story: As a user, I want to pause live capture without tearing down the connection so resume is fast.
Expected Behavior: Pausing suspends real audio while keeping the transcription socket warm, freezes elapsed time, and resuming continues capture without a full restart.

User Story: As a user, I want to mute my mic leg without stopping the entire session.
Expected Behavior: Mute state is user-controlled, affects only the mic leg, stays separate from system audio, and is surfaced from session commands.

User Story: As a user, I want RTI to ignore accidental automatic restarts immediately after I stop a session.
Expected Behavior: After a stop, automatic non-user-initiated starts are blocked during a short cooldown and while finalization is still in progress.

User Story: As a user, I want a clear error if session start fails because the mic permission is denied.
Expected Behavior: A denied permission leaves the session stopped, records a user-facing error, and opens the permission guidance path instead of silently failing.

User Story: As a user, I want RTI to go live on top of a meeting already being recorded by Meeting Sentinel.
Expected Behavior: When Sentinel reports a live meeting, the banner shows meeting name, elapsed time, a Brief button, and a Go live button that starts RTI linked to that meeting and opens the overlay.

User Story: As a user, I want a compact live transcript inside the overlay so I can follow what RTI is hearing without leaving the meeting.
Expected Behavior: The overlay transcript tab groups consecutive entries by speaker, shows health state and interim text, preserves prior originals when translation is enabled later, and supports copy-all.

User Story: As a user, I want a larger transcript window with health, mode, and translation controls for fuller monitoring.
Expected Behavior: The live transcript window shows connection health, elapsed time, mode picker, translation bar, transcript paragraphs, interim text, and copy-all behavior.

User Story: As a user, I want to translate live speech so I can follow multilingual conversations.
Expected Behavior: Translation can be turned on or off from transcript surfaces and commands; changing it updates SessionCoordinator translationConfig and reconnects transcription without clearing prior transcript history.
Entry Points: Overlay transcript; live transcript window; menu

User Story: As a user, I want one-way and two-way translation with explicit language controls.
Expected Behavior: Translation UI supports one-way target language or two-way language A/B selection; two-way mode exposes both sides and warns when the same language is chosen in the larger transcript surface.

User Story: As a user, I want to pick a client or project so RTI can ground answers in the right workstream.
Expected Behavior: Setup loads project and client items from the vault, filters them in one picker, stores the chosen workstream, shows a using banner, and renders the retrieved workstream context until cleared.

User Story: As a user, I want to write a freeform note about the meeting so the assistant can use extra context not found in the vault.
Expected Behavior: Setup persists a meeting note in memory and includes it as part of meeting context for later LLM turns.

User Story: As a user, I want to open Hermes-authored pre-meeting briefs from within RTI.
Expected Behavior: RTI locates recent briefs in the vault, lists them in a split view, reloads on demand, and shows an empty state until briefs exist.
Entry Points: Command palette; Sentinel banner; sessions window

Feature: Discussion guide import from project vault
User Story: As a user, I want RTI to discover discussion guides already attached to the selected project.
Expected Behavior: When the chosen workstream is a project, Setup lists guide files found in that project and allows loading them into the parser preview.

User Story: As a user, I want to add a discussion guide from pasted text or an uploaded file.
Expected Behavior: Setup supports pasted guide text plus upload of markdown, text, docx, doc, pdf, rtf, and html sources, extracting text and parsing it into a preview.

User Story: As a user, I want to preview the parsed guide before it becomes active so I can catch parser mistakes.
Expected Behavior: Parsed guides become pending first, showing objective and section structure; the user can confirm, discard, or later remove the active guide.

User Story: As a user, I want RTI to show which discussion-guide questions have been answered during the meeting.
Expected Behavior: If a guide is active, the Guide tab shows coverage stats and structured objective sections; otherwise it shows an empty state instructing the user to attach a guide from Setup.

User Story: As a user, I want to turn Notes on only when I need it so the extra live analysis stays opt-in.
Expected Behavior: Notes is off by default, becomes available as a live panel toggle, and when enabled adds the Notes tab and lets the scheduler generate note batches during the session.

User Story: As a user, I want to manually regenerate, copy, and export generated notes.
Expected Behavior: The Notes tab shows progress, errors, note blocks with time ranges, copy-per-block, copy-all, regenerate-now, and export-to-markdown actions.

User Story: As a user, I want to turn the Findings ledger on when I want a running list of tensions and missed threads.
Expected Behavior: Findings is opt-in, appears as a live panel toggle, and when enabled adds a Findings tab backed by scheduled generation.
Notes: Manual check on 2026-06-30: toggling Findings on immediately added the Findings tab; toggling it back off removed the tab.

User Story: As a user, I want to inspect, copy, and export tagged findings during a call.
Expected Behavior: The Findings tab shows tagged entries with timestamps, optional quotes and speakers, manual rescan, copy-per-entry, copy-all, and markdown export.

User Story: As a user, I want RTI to proactively surface suggestions only when I opt into that behavior.
Expected Behavior: Auto is opt-in, appears as a live panel toggle, and when enabled schedules proactive card generation plus quiet-window debounced generation after speech settles.

User Story: As a user, I want live proactive suggestions about what to say, ask, recall, or flag.
Expected Behavior: The Auto tab shows SAY, ASK, RECALL, and FLAG cards, manual resurface, copy support, and unseen-count semantics when the user has not viewed the tab.

User Story: As a user, I want to type my own question to RTI instead of relying only on canned actions.
Expected Behavior: The overlay composer accepts freeform text, submits on Return, clears draft on session stop, and routes the text through the standard LLM pipeline.

User Story: As a user, I want RTI to suggest what I should say next.
Expected Behavior: The Assist action sends the current prompt-store Assist prompt, grounded in recent transcript and meeting context, and streams a response into the chat.
Entry Points: Overlay actions menu; Command-Return; command palette

User Story: As a user, I want a terse one-line draft reply.
Expected Behavior: The Say Next action is available as a quick action and global hotkey and requests a one-line reply through the assistant pipeline.

User Story: As a user, I want RTI to propose follow-up questions based on the conversation.
Expected Behavior: The Follow-ups action uses its prompt-store prompt, includes guide coverage context when present, and streams results in chat.

Feature: Recap quick action and recap depth
User Story: As a user, I want fast recaps at different levels of detail.
Expected Behavior: RTI offers Recap as an action, persists a sticky recap depth, and also supports brief and detailed one-shot recap variants via commands.
Entry Points: Overlay actions menu; Command-Option-R; command palette

User Story: As a user, I want RTI to generate a full meeting summary over the complete transcript so far.
Expected Behavior: The Session Summary action forces the smart model and runs over the full transcript window rather than the recent context slice.

User Story: As a passive observer, I want RTI to switch from speaking advice to observation-centric research prompts.
Expected Behavior: Listener mode exposes Key Tensions, What's Unsaid or Probe, and Emerging Themes actions and adjusts Assist and Follow-ups framing for observer sessions.
Entry Points: Overlay actions menu; command palette; hotkeys

User Story: As a user, I want Command-Return to run the quick action I use most.
Expected Behavior: The primary action can be remapped to any eligible assistant action, persists in user defaults, and is reflected in the actions menu and command surfaces.

User Story: As a user, I want to toggle reasoning-heavy responses when the extra latency is worth it.
Expected Behavior: Smart mode persists to user defaults and flips the LLM pipeline into smart-mode requests unless a given action already forces smart behavior.
Entry Points: Menu; command palette; overlay actions menu indicator

User Story: As a user, I want to wipe the current chat transcript without touching the live meeting transcript.
Expected Behavior: Clearing chat cancels any in-flight stream, removes in-memory assistant entries immediately, and hides auxiliary floating panels without a confirmation modal.
Entry Points: Menu; overlay more menu; command palette

User Story: As a user, I want to see when RTI is still thinking or using a tool and stop it if needed.
Expected Behavior: While a response streams, the chat tracks streaming and reasoning state plus tool status; the composer swaps send for stop and cancellation prunes empty assistant output.

User Story: As a user, I want to switch LLM providers without restarting RTI so the next assistant turn uses a different backend immediately.
Expected Behavior: Assistant provider selection persists, is exposed in Providers settings plus menu and overlay quick-switch surfaces, and the next LLM request resolves the newly active provider at call time.
Entry Points: Settings > Providers; menu; overlay more menu
Notes: Overlay More-actions menu shows Assistant provider and Transcription provider submenus on fresh app process 2026-06-30.

User Story: As a user, I want to flip between normal chat and a quick note insert mode with almost no friction.
Expected Behavior: The Assist composer shows a visible `Chat`/`Note` toggle during a live session, keeps focus in the field when toggled, inserts note text inline into the transcript on Enter, and then returns to chat mode automatically for one-off notes.
Notes: UX change implemented 2026-06-30; manual pass still pending.

Feature: Context capture by hotkey or menu
User Story: As a user, I want to attach OCR from the current screen to my next assistant turn.
Expected Behavior: Capture Screen runs from command surfaces, uses screenshot plus OCR services, and stores extracted text as pending screen context for the next LLM message rather than sending raw images to the model.
Entry Points: Command-Shift-H; overlay more menu; command palette

User Story: As a user, I want to drop an image onto the composer to extract text into the next message.
Expected Behavior: The overlay composer accepts dropped images, OCRs them on-device, and attaches extracted text as pending screen context.

User Story: As a user, I want to change assistant mode mid-meeting so the next response follows a different system prompt or reference context.
Expected Behavior: Modes can be switched from the overlay, live transcript window, or command surfaces, and the next LLM turn uses the active mode without restarting the session.
Entry Points: Overlay more menu; live transcript window; command palette

User Story: As a user, I want to create, edit, activate, and delete custom modes.
Expected Behavior: Settings list built-in and custom modes, support add and save, block deletion of built-ins, and allow system prompt plus reference text editing.

User Story: As a user, I want to edit the shipped prompts that RTI uses for different actions.
Expected Behavior: Settings organize prompts by group, show edited status and changed-default warnings, allow save, revert, reset-one, reset-all, and preview assembled recap prompts.
Notes: Manual smoke pass on 2026-06-30: integrated prompt library, grouped list, editor, and export/reset controls render and are navigable in Sessions Control.

User Story: As a user, I want to export the current shipped prompt defaults for offline comparison or prompt-lab work.
Expected Behavior: Settings can write a JSON export of shipped defaults to a user-selected location and surface errors with a native alert.

User Story: As a user, I want to maintain a glossary of names and terms so RTI preserves them across LLM outputs.
Expected Behavior: Settings allow multiline glossary editing, ignore comment headers, parse term lines, and show whether parsed entries are currently being sent with every LLM call.
Notes: Manual smoke pass on 2026-06-30: glossary instructions, editable text area, and parsed-entry status surface render correctly in unified control.

User Story: As a user, I want to choose which speech-to-text provider RTI uses.
Expected Behavior: Setup and Providers settings expose provider selection, persist the active provider, and a live change reconnects the streaming client with a short gap; if AssemblyAI is selected without its key, RTI falls back to Soniox.
Notes: Manual verification confirmed provider radios in Providers settings and provider submenus in overlay More-actions on 2026-06-30.

User Story: As a user, I want one settings surface for both provider selection and stored credentials so swapping models is simple.
Expected Behavior: The Providers tab combines assistant-provider selection, STT-provider selection, and stored keys for all supported providers, with provider-specific missing-key guidance and no separate assistant/transcription provider sections in General. The Sessions Control workspace now exposes those settings pages directly in its main left rail instead of treating them as a nested settings-within-settings shell.
Entry Points: Sessions Control > Providers / Modes / Prompts / Glossary / General; Settings command
Notes: Unified control navigation implemented 2026-06-30; `WindowCoordinator.openSettings()` now lands on the integrated Providers page in Sessions Control.

User Story: As a user, I want a separate provider choice for future transcript upgrades so I can use a better batch provider than the live one.
Expected Behavior: Providers settings distinguish `Real-time speech-to-text` from `Transcript upgrade (async)`, persist the async provider separately, and store any async-only credentials such as Aliyun without affecting the live lane.
Notes: Architecture split added on 2026-06-30; current app ships settings/docs, not the Upgrade Transcript job itself.

User Story: As a user, I want to pick the microphone or virtual device RTI should use.
Expected Behavior: Settings list system default plus available input devices, persist a preferred input UID, and apply it on the next session.

User Story: As a user, I want to optionally enable acoustic echo cancellation when I am on speakers.
Expected Behavior: Settings persist an echo-cancellation preference, explain the current risk of silent microphones on some Macs, and apply the choice on the next session.

User Story: As a user, I want RTI to avoid lowering my Bluetooth headphone volume during capture.
Expected Behavior: Settings expose a persisted toggle that keeps Bluetooth headphones at full volume by favoring the built-in mic during recording and restoring the earlier mic on stop.

User Story: As a user, I want RTI to open automatically when I log into my Mac.
Expected Behavior: Settings reflect the current launch-at-login state, attempt to change it, and restore the previous toggle plus surface an error if the change fails.

User Story: As a user, I want to verify that RTI is capturing both my side and the other party before or during a meeting.
Expected Behavior: Settings embed a live audio monitor with current device and level information; the same monitor is also available from the menubar.

User Story: As a user, I want a single place to confirm RTI's global shortcuts.
Expected Behavior: Settings list the principal global hotkeys and explain that Command-Return is remappable while additional quick AI actions live in the command palette.

User Story: As a user, I want quick access to RTI's support folder, crash log, and logs.
Expected Behavior: Settings can reveal the RTI Application Support folder, reveal a crash log if one exists, and route to the logs viewer.

User Story: As a user, I want to copy a concise diagnostics bundle for support or debugging.
Expected Behavior: Settings surface version, model, and provider diagnostics and can copy a formatted diagnostics block to the pasteboard.

User Story: As a developer or operator, I want clear documentation for live transcription versus future transcript upgrades so provider choices and summary regeneration behavior are unambiguous.
Expected Behavior: Docs explain that real-time STT and async transcript upgrade are separate lanes, recommend provider defaults per lane, and describe how a future Upgrade Transcript action should regenerate the summary from upgraded text.
Notes: Documentation added 2026-06-30 and tied to the transcribe skill’s provider defaults.

User Story: As a user, I want to inspect RTI's current and past application logs without opening files manually.
Expected Behavior: The logs window switches between live in-memory entries and past daily files, supports copy, clear or reveal actions appropriate to each mode, and shows the crash log in an expandable section.
Notes: Manual smoke pass on 2026-06-30: verified live/past toggle, past-date selector, copy/reveal controls, and crash-log disclosure inside Sessions Control.

User Story: As a user, I want to read past RTI sessions inside the app after they are saved.
Expected Behavior: The Sessions browser loads recent archive folders, groups them by date buckets, opens a selected session, and defaults to the highest-priority available file.
Entry Points: Sessions window > Sessions; notifications; overlay more menu

User Story: As a user, I want to copy or export archived session files for sharing or further work outside RTI.
Expected Behavior: The Sessions browser can copy the current markdown, export markdown, export PDF, and reveal the backing session folder in Finder.

User Story: As a user, I want RTI to preserve text artifacts from a finished session without keeping audio.
Expected Behavior: On stop, RTI can write transcript, chat, notes, discussion-guide, findings, and summary artifacts into a timestamped session folder with owner-only permissions; live translation tokens are excluded from the kept transcript.

User Story: As a user, I want a notification when the post-stop summary is ready and a direct path into that session.
Expected Behavior: When auto-summary finishes, RTI posts a local notification carrying the session folder; clicking it activates RTI and opens that exact session in the browser.

User Story: As a user, I want any retained session audio to live beside the transcript and summary so the session folder is self-contained for upgrades and review.
Expected Behavior: When a session is archived, any kept `mic` and `system` `.m4a` files are moved into that session folder as `audio-mic.m4a` and `audio-system.m4a` on a best-effort basis.
Notes: Forward path implemented 2026-06-30; retroactive migration for old recordings remains to be done conservatively.
